atomicity.reason: Three related aspects in one requirement: writing one record per fault to non-volatile memory, the three mandated content fields, and readability over the diagnostic interface after a power cycle. The retrieval path is separable from the write, though all three are facets of one recording obligation.
atomicity.suggestion: Keep the write obligation and its mandated fields here, and move post-power-cycle read-back over the diagnostic interface into its own requirement.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained - it names the storage, the three fields and the retrieval path without relying on an adjacent requirement.

feasibility.reason: A small non-volatile record per fault with a diagnostic read service; standard practice and consistent with the fault-memory architecture element.

parent_fit.reason: Delivers the parent story's observable that the workshop sees a stored fault entry naming the cell and the limit it crossed, and adds the measured value.

unambiguity.reason: 'one fault record per cell-protection fault' does not settle repeated violations of the same limit, nor what happens when the memory is full, so the expected record count for a recurring fault has more than one reading.
unambiguity.suggestion: Define what constitutes one fault occurrence (e.g. one record per entry into the latched state) and the overflow policy when non-volatile memory is full.

verifiability.reason: Concrete test: force a fault, power-cycle, read the record back and check the three named fields against the injected values.

summary: Content fields are well chosen and match the parent's workshop observable, but the requirement bundles the retrieval path with the write, and leaves repeat-fault and memory-full behaviour open.
